info.title: Nyanbin API
info.description:
Nyanbin is a zero-knowledge pastebin. All encryption and decryption happens
on the client; the server only ever stores an **opaque envelope** and can
never read note contents or passwords. Delete tokens are transient bearer
capabilities: the server generates or receives them when required but
never logs or stores them; only their SHA-256 digests are persisted.

## Creating a note: reserve → encrypt → commit

1. `POST /api/notes/reserve` with the desired lifecycle. The server mints a
   note ID, a `deleteToken` capability, and the authoritative lifecycle
   (`expiresAt` in milliseconds since the Unix epoch, optional `maxReads`).
2. The client encrypts the note **locally** into a protocol-v1 envelope and
   binds the returned lifecycle into it.
3. `PUT /api/notes/{id}` commits the envelope together with the **same**
   lifecycle and the SHA-256 hex digest of the delete token.

A reservation lives for the instance-configured reservation TTL (10–600
seconds; 120 seconds by default). If it is not committed in time it
silently expires and the ID is never published.

## Idempotency and retries

Reserve is **not idempotent**: a lost response is harmless (the unused
reservation simply expires) and the correct retry is a fresh reserve call.
Commit is naturally safe to retry against races: a second commit to the
same ID is rejected with `409 reservation_mismatch`, so at most one
envelope is ever published per reservation. There is **no
idempotency-key mechanism** and none is needed.

## The envelope is opaque

The `envelope` field is canonical base64url produced only by the published
protocol implementation (npm package `nyanbin`, export
`./shared/protocol`). Clients **must not** send plaintext or ad-hoc
ciphertext; the server validates canonical envelope framing but by design
cannot inspect the contents.

## Reading is consuming

`POST /api/notes/{id}/reveal` atomically burns one read **before** the
client decrypts anything locally. If the note is password protected and
the reader enters a wrong password, the read is already consumed — clients
must not blindly retry reveals. Use `GET /api/notes/{id}` (metadata only,
non-consuming) to inspect lifecycle and remaining reads.

## Delete tokens are capabilities

Deletion requires presenting the original `deleteToken`. The server stores
only its SHA-256 hex digest, so a database leak does not leak the
capability itself.

## Short links

Short codes are only issued for **password-protected** notes, because a
short code is guessable and the password is the remaining secret. Requests
for unprotected notes fail with `409 short_link_requires_password`.

## Rate limits and storage pressure

All `429 rate_limited` responses carry a `Retry-After` header (integer
seconds, at least 1). This includes the per-client hourly upload byte
quota, whose `Retry-After` points at the next hour boundary.

Under storage pressure the service browns out gracefully: near the storage
budget, large commits are rejected with `507 storage_pressure`; when the
budget is effectively full, all commits are rejected with `507`. Reads,
reveals, and deletes keep working throughout.

## Operator kill switches

Operators can temporarily disable subsets of the API. These conditions
surface as `503 writes_disabled` (reserve and commit paused),
`503 short_disabled` (short-link create/resolve paused), or a
restriction of large commits to `507 storage_pressure`. They are
temporary operational measures, not permanent API changes.

## Versioning

`info.version` tracks the public API surface (v1), decoupled from the
application's own release version reported by `GET /api/status`. See the
published stability policy for compatibility guarantees: the wire
`protocol` field governs cryptographic compatibility, while this HTTP
surface governs transport compatibility.

post.summary: Reserve a note ID and delete token
post.description:
Mints a fresh note ID, a `deleteToken` capability, and the
authoritative lifecycle. The reservation lives for the
instance-configured TTL (10–600 seconds; 120 seconds by default);
commit promptly or the ID silently expires.

Reserve is **not idempotent**. If the response is lost, simply
reserve again — the abandoned reservation expires harmlessly and is
never published.

In the request, omitting `maxReads` applies the instance default and
an explicit `0` requests unlimited reads. In the response lifecycle,
`maxReads` is either a positive count or absent (unlimited) — never 0.

400.description: Malformed request (`invalid_request`, `invalid_json`) or lifecycle outside the instance limits (`invalid_lifecycle`).

503.description: Writes temporarily paused by the operator (`writes_disabled`), backing store unreachable (`storage_unavailable`), or no free ID could be minted (`id_space_exhausted`). All are temporary; retry later.

put.summary: Commit an encrypted envelope to a reservation
put.description:
Publishes the note by attaching the locally encrypted envelope to a
prior reservation. The lifecycle **must equal** the lifecycle returned
by reserve, and `deleteTokenHash` must be the SHA-256 hex digest of
the reserved delete token. Commit transmits only that digest, not the
raw token.

The envelope is opaque canonical base64url produced by the published
protocol implementation (npm package `nyanbin`, export
`./shared/protocol`). Never send plaintext.

Commit is safe against duplicate delivery: a second commit to the same
ID yields `409 reservation_mismatch`, so at most one envelope is ever
published per reservation.

400.description: Malformed request (`invalid_request`, `invalid_json`), malformed ID (`invalid_id`), lifecycle mismatch or out of range (`invalid_lifecycle`), or non-canonical envelope (`invalid_envelope`).

404.description: Reservation expired or unknown (`reservation_not_found`). Reserve again.

409.description: Commit does not match the reservation, or an envelope was already committed for this ID (`reservation_mismatch`).

413.description: Envelope exceeds the instance size limit (`payload_too_large`).

503.description: Writes temporarily paused by the operator (`writes_disabled`) or backing store unreachable (`storage_unavailable`).

507.description: Storage pressure brownout (`storage_pressure`): near the storage budget only small commits are accepted; at the budget all commits are rejected. Temporary; retry later or with a smaller note.

get.description:
Returns lifecycle metadata and whether the note is password protected
**without** consuming a read. Use this to inspect `remainingReads`
before revealing.

404.description: Note unknown, expired, or fully consumed (`note_not_found`).

delete.summary: Delete a note with its delete token
delete.description:
Deletes the note when the presented `deleteToken` matches the SHA-256
digest stored at commit time. The token is a bearer capability: the
server never stores it in the clear.

403.description: Delete token is malformed or does not match (`invalid_delete_token`).

404.description: Note unknown, expired, or fully consumed (`note_not_found`).

post.description:
Returns the encrypted envelope and **atomically burns one read** —
the burn happens on the server before any local decryption. If the
note is password protected and the reader supplies a wrong password
afterwards, the read is already consumed; clients must not blindly
retry reveals. Once the last read is consumed the note is gone and
subsequent requests return 404.

404.description: Note unknown, expired, or fully consumed (`note_not_found`).

post.summary: Create or fetch a short code for a note
post.description:
Issues a 6-character short code for a **password-protected** note.
Requires the note's delete token as proof of ownership. Returns 201
with a fresh code, or 200 with the existing code if one was already
issued. Notes without password protection are refused with
`409 short_link_requires_password`, because a short code is guessable
and the password must remain as the protecting secret.

403.description: Delete token is malformed or does not match (`invalid_delete_token`).

404.description: Note unknown, expired, or fully consumed (`note_not_found`).

503.description: Short links temporarily paused by the operator (`short_disabled`), backing store unreachable (`storage_unavailable`), or no free code could be allocated (`short_code_space_exhausted`). All are temporary; retry later.

get.summary: Resolve a short code to a note ID
get.description:
Resolves a short code to the full note ID. Resolution is
non-consuming; reading the note still requires the reveal endpoint
and the note's password.

404.description: Unknown short code or expired note (`note_not_found`).

503.description: Short links temporarily paused by the operator (`short_disabled`) or backing store unreachable (`storage_unavailable`).

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying (integer, at least 1).

RateLimited.description: Too many requests (`rate_limited`). Also returned when the per-client hourly upload byte quota is exhausted; then `Retry-After` points at the next hour boundary.

Lifecycle.description: Authoritative note lifecycle. `maxReads` is a positive count or absent for unlimited reads — never 0.

expiresAt.description: Expiry as milliseconds since the Unix epoch (uint64).

maxReads.description: Maximum read count; absent means unlimited. Never 0.

deleteToken.description: Delete capability: base64url of 32 random bytes. Shown once; the server stores only its SHA-256 digest after commit.
